question: Long chain compounds formed by Silicon are ______________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Very reactive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Non-metallic chemical element **silicon (Si)** is a **member of the carbon family**.
 
• The **octahedral crystalline structure** of pure silicon is a** hard, dark grey solid with a metallic lustre**.
 
• Since** pure silicon** is too reactive to be found in nature, it is instead mixed with other elements or oxygen to **form silica**, which is present in almost all **rocks, sand, clays, and soils**.
 
• the **long chain compounds** formed by silicon are **very reactive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity** is the** ease with which one substance reacts chemically with another**.
 
• The** arrangement of metals in descending order of their reactivities **is referred to as the** "metal reactivity series"**, sometimes known as the **"activity series"**.
 
• The** susceptibility of an anion to become polarised by a cation** is known as **polarizability**. When the **degree of polarization is very low**, an** ionic bond** is created, and when it is** very high**, a** covalent bond** is created.
